P1 — The logarithmic covariance bound needs a sample-size qualification — Counterevidence and scope: The proof uses p=ceil(ln n), requiring p>=1. The n>=2 argument inspected on pp.20-23 uses valid rank, moment, and quadratic estimates. Programmatic convention search over all 27 pages, followed by reading the relevant notation and hits, found no global n>=2 or truncated-log convention. The defect is confined to the finite endpoint; it does not refute the intended asymptotic rates. Corollary 2.9 at n=1 can be bounded directly by 2 E||X|| and its Gaussian term, so it is not additionally alleged false.

proposition.claim:
For probability measures on Euclidean space, the paper’s max-sliced distance is \[W_{p,1}(\mu,\nu)=
 \sup_{\|v\|_2=1}W_p\bigl((\langle v,\cdot\rangle)_\#\mu,
                         (\langle v,\cdot\rangle)_\#\nu\bigr).\] The more general \(W_{1,s}\) of Section 1.3 uses \(s\) coordinate functionals in the dual unit ball; their mutual orthogonality is not an assumption. In the Banach-space results, separability of the dual and the first-moment assumption are retained. In the Hilbert-space moment bounds, the stated \(2+\delta\) or \(2+2\delta\) moments are required where they occur, with \(0<\delta\leq1\). The centered lower bounds require \(\mathbb E X=0\); centering is not silently imposed on the upper bounds.

Equation reference: eq:original. Theorem 1.4 assumes a symmetric probability measure on \(\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\|x\|_2\leq r\}\), where \(r>0\), and independent samples \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) with that law. Write \[\nu_n=\frac1{2n}\sum_{i=1}^n(\delta_{X_i}+\delta_{-X_i}),
 \qquad
 \Sigma=\mathbb E XX^{T},\qquad \kappa=\|\Sigma\|_{\rm op}.\] For \(\kappa>0\), its asserted upper bound is equivalently \[
 \mathbb E W_{2,1}(\mu,\nu_n)^2
 \leq C\left(\frac{r^2\log n}{n}
       +r\sqrt{\frac{\kappa\log n}{n}}\right).\] Neither copy of the theorem, on pages 6 and 22, explicitly states \(n\geq2\). The counterexample below uses \(\kappa>0\) and does not exploit division by zero or an inadmissible distribution.
